headlines.text: That Wednesday in 2023, Orange Cassidy vs. Jeff Jarrett etched their names into history in the first-ever AEW International Title match, appearing on Dynamite, rated 6.42. In the final defense of the AEW All-Atlantic Championship before its rebrand, Cassidy fought off interference from Jarrett's entire crew to retain and become the first-ever AEW International Champion.

Flash back to 2026, when the AEW World Heavyweight Title was up for grabs as MJF vs. Adam Page went to war in a Texas Death Match, appearing on Revolution, rated 8.98 ? a genuine showstealer. It marked Adam Page's 20th match with the title on the line. In an unhinged Texas Death Match with Page's very ability to ever challenge for the title again on the line, MJF survived a savage ten-count brawl to retain the AEW World Championship.
Rewind to 2025, when FTR vs. O'Reilly & Strong headlined Collision, rated 7.88 ? a solid showing in a physical tag team battle.

secondaries.text: Back on this day in 2024, AEW welcomed Uno & Silver for the first time as a team, appearing on Rampage, rated 5.80.

Rewind to 2026, when Jon Moxley vs. Konosuke Takeshita clashed for the AEW Continental Title, appearing on Revolution, rated 8.68 ? a stone-cold classic. It was the 20th time the AEW Continental Title had been on the line, a nice marker in that championship's story. In a first-ever No Time Limit meeting, Moxley choked out Takeshita with a grapevine rear naked choke to retain the Continental Title in a war that took every ounce of both men.

Back on this day in 2026, FTR vs. The Young Bucks clashed for the AEW World Tag Team Titles, appearing on Revolution, rated 9.17 ? a match fans still talk about. FTR retained the AEW World Tag Team Titles over the Young Bucks with an Avalanche Shatter Machine, the veterans once again proving too much for the EVPs.
